title: How can we turn a triangle into a rectangle of the same area?
description: A triangle is cut at half its height by joining the midpoints of two sides. The top triangle is split by its height, and the two halves turn about the midpoints to fill the gaps and make a rectangle on the same base.
teaching_notes: One idea: cutting at half the height and turning the top pieces makes a rectangle with the same base and half the height. Watch for students who forget the half in the area of a triangle.

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 6, Sulba Sutras)
video_script.why: The child uses cut and turn from the solved example to dissect a triangle into a rectangle of the same area.
video_script.substitution: Cut at half the height and turn the top pieces down.
video_script.anchor: the book's triangle ABC with the midpoints D and E
video_script.payoff_line: Cut at half the height and turn the top pieces to make a rectangle

final_answer.value: cut at half the height and turn the top pieces to make a rectangle on the base with half the height
final_answer.spoken: cut at half the height and turn the top pieces to make a rectangle

maths_rules: D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC; DE is parallel to BC at half the height
AM is the height from A to DE; the half turn about D sends A to B, since D is the midpoint of AB; the half turn about E sends A to C
the turned pieces fill the gaps beside BD and CE; the rectangle has base BC and height half of the triangle's height
video_script.design: One triangle all video: two cuts and two turns make a rectangle.
open_questions: The worklist says to drop perpendiculars from the midpoints to the base and turn the top pieces down. Dropping perpendiculars from D and E gives a rectangle only half as wide as BC. The video instead cuts the top triangle along its height and turns the two halves about D and E, which fills the gaps beside BD and CE exactly.
